stories.title: PM Shehbaz vows to strengthen Maldives ties for 'all time to come'; 20 MoUs signed
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday vowed to strengthen bilateral relations with the Maldives, as the two countries signed 20 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) during the visit of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu.
Concluding his remarks, PM Shehbaz said Muizzu’s visit had given Pakistan-Maldives relations “new purpose and new momentum”.
Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, FO said.

stories.title: 10 killed, 44 injured as passenger bus overturns on highway in Punjab's Rajanpur
summary: DERA GHAZI KHAN: Ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil, Rescue 1122 said.

Of the 44 wounded, 38 were being treated at the Rajanpur District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital, while four critically injured persons were referred to Dera Ghazi Khan and two seriously hurt to Rahim Yar Khan’s Sheikh Zayed Hospital.
Rescue 1122 said it “responded promptly” upon receiving the emergency call and mobilised 10 ambulances and two rescue vehicles from Rajanpur, Jampur and Rojhan.

stories.title: US envoy to meet Putin after 'positive' talks with Zelensky
summary: Washington’s envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine.
After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.
Trump has also been keeping up the pressure on Ukraine, saying at the White House that he wanted Zelensky to “make a deal” with Russia, which is ramping up its strikes as a bitter winter looms.

stories.title: ECP orders fresh schedule for Islamabad local government polls
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday directed its office to prepare and issue the election programme for local government elections in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday ruled that Islamabad local government (LG) elections would be conducted under the ICT Local Government Act, 2015, adding that it would issue a schedule for the polls later in the day.

stories.title: Profit rates on National Savings schemes increased from Oct 21
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has increased profit rates on several national savings schemes, including those for pensioners, senior citizens and families of martyrs, with the revised rates taking effect from October 21.

According to the revised schedule issued by the Central Directorate of National Savings (CDNS), the profit rate on Behbood Savings Certificates, Pensioners’ Benefit Accounts and Shuhada’s Family Welfare Accounts has been raised to 12.96 per cent from 12.72pc.
The profit rate on Special Savings Certificates has been increased to 12pc from 11.6pc for the first five profit payments.

stories.title: ATHLETICS: PATHS TO GLORY
summary: Pakistani triathletes Sana Arif (left) and Anisha Ali at the competition venue of the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan | Courtesy Sana Arif For Sana Arif, the journey to the Asian Games began with a sport she had only learnt a few years earlier.
For Pakistan’s first women triathletes at the Asian Games, the competition was about more than medals.

Pakistan was sending women triathletes to compete at the continental Games, and Sana and Anisha would be part of a small pioneering team, entering a competition in which the country had never before had female representation.

stories.title: Fear as Indians struggle to prove voting rights
summary: Laddli Khatun pulled one document after another from a yellow bag, desperately hoping one would be enough to keep her name on India’s electoral rolls.
The Election Commission previously sought to enrol eligible voters through door-to-door visits, guided by its motto: “No voter to be left behind”.

However, Indian media have reported cases in West Bengal in which people excluded from voter rolls were accused of being undocumented migrants from Bangladesh, detained and, in some instances, pushed across the border.

stories.title: SC issues notices to KP IG prisons, ACS for not complying with its order
summary: PESHAWAR: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued show cause notices to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa inspector general of prisons and the additional chief secretary (home), directing them to appear in person today (Wednesday) to explain their position for not complying with its order.

stories.title: Karachi hospital sealed for negligence after infant contracts mpox
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh Healthcare Commission (SHCC) has sealed a private hospital in Malir after receiving a report from the district health officer (DHO) about a laboratory-confirmed mpox case in an infant.

Following the report, SHCC officials, with the support of the DHO Korangi and the SSP, took action and sealed the hospital, which was being run illegally by non-qualified staff and quacks,” said the statement.

stories.title: Mine owners seek lifting of explosives ban in KP

Mr Tanoli said the minerals department had been subjected to politically motivated criticism for several years and had faced hundreds of inquiries and National Accountability Bureau (NAB) cases over the past two decades.
Mr Tanoli said illegal mining remained a serious challenge for the provincial government.

stories.title: Sooryavanshi told to be patient by Iyer
summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi "can't just walk straight into the team", India captain Shreyas Iyer said Wednesday, after calls for the teenage sensation to be unleashed for the T20 series against New Zealand starting in Christchurch this week.

stories.title: Senate committee reviews proposed changes to General Cosmetics Bill
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Science and Technology on Tuesday reviewed proposed amendments to the Pakistan General Cosmetics Bill, 2026.
The committee stressed the need for effective regulation of cosmetic products, action against counterfeiting and safeguards against the misuse of regulatory powers.

The committee observed the bill should establish a transparent and workable regulatory system that curb counterfeit products, protect consumers from unsafe cosmetics and provides clear standards for legitimate businesses.

stories.title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency
summary: UEFA has sent a letter to FIFA seeking answers by November 2 about Gianni Infantino's presidency, including questions over the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and the FIFA Peace Prize.

The 56-year-old, who is up for reelection next year, apologised to the FIFA Council last week and told attendees to ⁠submit any questions they had about his governance in writing so he could answer them at the next meeting on December 16.
"The FIFA Governance Regulations state that Council meetings and their associated documentation are confidential," a spokesperson for world soccer's governing body FIFA said on Tuesday.

stories.title: Season of uprisings

stories.title: Minhas terms England performance 'memorable'
summary: Pakistan all-rounder Arafat Minhas described his performance against England as a memorable day after scoring 59 runs and taking six wickets for 40 runs in an outstanding display with bat and ball.

stories.title: A rubber-stamp parliament
summary: Last week, both Houses of parliament approved, within hours and by a two-thirds majority, the decision to remove an elected provincial government and impose a state of emergency and governor’s rule, with no substantive debate.

But a question that is never answered is whether the state has a well-defined, overarching counterterrorism policy in place, and, if it does, whether that policy has ever been discussed in cabinet, let alone presented before parliament or any of its committees for deliberation.

stories.title: Landmark biodiversity fund collapses with just $7,085 raised

stories.title: BYD to rely on imports initially, Hubco says
summary: KARACHI: Hub Power Company (Hubco) has said that BYD vehicle production will initially rely entirely on imported raw materials and components, with localisation increasing gradually over time.
The management is targeting an initial sales run rate of approximately 1,000-1,500 BYD vehicles per month as production ramps up.

stories.title: CDF Munir-Pezeshkian meeting raises peace hopes
summary: ISLAMABAD: Iranian leaders have told Pakistan that the United States must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations.
